description: Verify that DUT discards a UDP datagram whose Length field is smaller than the actual data on the wire (RFC 768 'Format' + automotive frame integrity)
approach:
[Objective]
If UDP.Length < (actual bytes on the wire), the receiver would silently truncate the payload — discarding bytes that the sender intended to deliver. For automotive flows where every byte may be load-bearing, RFC 768's Format rule plus the TC8 frame-integrity stance require the datagram to be dropped entirely. (Companion of FIELDS_10 which covers the over-claim direction.)

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: UDP datagram with Length field intentionally smaller than actual bytes

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester must NOT receive the datagram (UT-query confirms drop)

[Pass condition]
UT-query confirms DUT did not deliver the under-length UDP.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT delivered the under-length UDP (parser silently truncated)
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue)

verdicts.Pass: DUT discarded the under-length UDP — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT received UDP with Length smaller than actual data
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No UT confirmation for under-length discard
